)

library(tidyverse)
library(DT)
library(knitr)
library(plotly)
library(crosstalk)
library(gggenes)
library(kableExtra)
library(jsonlite)
library(ggrepel)

```

```{r sample_title, results='asis'}
# Add the sample name to the title.
cat(sprintf('---\ntitle: "Gene Origin Report: %s"\n---\n', snakemake@params[["sample"]]))
```

```{r load data}
# Load and process data from Bakta, EggNOG-mapper, ABRicate, geNomad, and MetaGraph outputs.

#Bakta
lines <- readLines(snakemake@input[["bakta_tsv"]])
header_line <- grep("^#Sequence", lines)
bakta_tsv <- read_tsv(
    paste(lines[header_line:length(lines)], collapse = "\n"),
    col_names = TRUE
) %>%
    rename_with(~ str_remove(., "^#"))

bakta_txt <- readLines(snakemake@input[["bakta_txt"]])
get_val <- function(key) {
  line <- grep(paste0("^\\s*", key, ":"), bakta_txt, value = TRUE)
  trimws(sub(".*:\\s*", "", line))
}

genome_length <- paste0(get_val("Length"), " bp")
gc_content <- paste0(get_val("GC"), " %")
coding_density <- paste0(get_val("coding density"), " %")
n_trna        <- get_val("tRNAs") 
n_tmrna        <- get_val("tmRNAs")
n_rrna        <- get_val("rRNAs")
n_ncrna        <- get_val("ncRNAs")
n_cds         <- get_val("CDSs")
n_pseudogenes <- get_val("pseudogenes")
n_hypothetical <- get_val("hypotheticals")
n_sorf <- get_val("sORFs")
n_orics <- get_val("oriCs")
n_orivs <- get_val("oriVs")
n_orits <- get_val("oriTs")
bakta_version <- get_val("Software")
db_version    <- get_val("Database")

#EggNOG
ann_lines <- readLines(snakemake@input[["eggnog_annotations"]])
emapper_version <- grep("^## emapper", ann_lines, value = TRUE) %>%
    str_extract("emapper-[\\d\\.]+-\\w+")
ann_header <- grep("^#query", ann_lines)
eggnog_ann <- read_tsv(
    paste(ann_lines[ann_header:length(ann_lines)], collapse = "\n"),
    comment = "##",
    col_names = TRUE
) %>%
    rename(query = `#query`)

orth_lines <- readLines(snakemake@input[["eggnog_orthologs"]]) 
orth_header <- grep("^#qseqid", orth_lines)
eggnog_orth <- read_tsv(
    paste(orth_lines[orth_header:length(orth_lines)], collapse = "\n"),
    comment = "##",
    col_names = TRUE
) %>%
    rename(query = `#qseqid`)

eggnog_combined <- eggnog_ann %>%
    left_join(
        eggnog_orth %>% select(query, sseqid, pident, qcov, scov),
        by = c("query", "seed_ortholog" = "sseqid")
    )

# Combined Bakta + EggNOG table for display, with column names prefixed by
# source since the two tools' columns are interleaved in one table.
bakta_eggnog_combined <- bakta_tsv %>%
    left_join(
        eggnog_combined %>%
            select(query, seed_ortholog, pident, qcov, scov, COG_category, Description),
        by = c("Locus Tag" = "query")
    ) %>%
    select(
        `Sequence Id`, `Locus Tag`, Type, Gene, Product,
        seed_ortholog, pident, qcov, scov, COG_category, Description
    ) %>%
    rename(
        `Bakta: Sequence Id`    = `Sequence Id`,
        `Bakta: Locus Tag`      = `Locus Tag`,
        `Bakta: Type`           = Type,
        `Bakta: Gene`           = Gene,
        `Bakta: Product`        = Product,
        `EggNOG: Seed ortholog` = seed_ortholog,
        `EggNOG: % identity`    = pident,
        `EggNOG: Query cov`     = qcov,
        `EggNOG: Subject cov`   = scov,
        `EggNOG: COG category`  = COG_category,
        `EggNOG: Description`   = Description
    )

#ABRicate
abricate_summary <- read_tsv(snakemake@input[["abricate_summary"]], comment = "",
        col_types = cols(.default = "c")) %>%
    mutate(`#FILE` = str_extract(`#FILE`, "abricate_(\\w+)\\.tab", group = 1)) %>%
    rename(Database = `#FILE`)

abricate_hits <- map_dfr(
    c(snakemake@input[["abricate_ncbi"]], 
        snakemake@input[["abricate_card"]], 
        snakemake@input[["abricate_resfinder"]],
        snakemake@input[["abricate_plasmidfinder"]]),
    function(f) {
        db_name <- str_extract(basename(f), "abricate_(\\w+)\\.tab", group = 1)
        # Fixed column types so files with no hits (header only) can be combined with the others.
        read_tsv(f, col_types = cols(START = "i", END = "i", .default = "c")) %>%
            mutate(source_db = db_name)
    }
)

abricate_hits_amr <- abricate_hits %>% filter(source_db != "PlasmidFinder")
abricate_hits_plasmid <- abricate_hits %>% filter(source_db == "PlasmidFinder")

abricate_mincov <- snakemake@params[["abricate_mincov"]]
abricate_minid  <- snakemake@params[["abricate_minid"]]

#GeNomad
genomad_virus <- read_tsv(snakemake@input[["genomad_virus"]])
genomad_plasmid <- read_tsv(snakemake@input[["genomad_plasmid"]])

genomad_regions <- bind_rows(
    # Coordinates are only given for proviruses; a whole-contig virus spans 1 to its length.
    if (nrow(genomad_virus) > 0) genomad_virus %>%
        mutate(origin = "Virus",
            coordinates = coalesce(as.character(coordinates), paste0("1-", length))) %>%
        select(seq_name, origin, coordinates, length, n_genes,
            any_of(c("virus_score", "taxonomy"))) %>%
        rename(score = virus_score),
    # geNomad plasmid summaries have no coordinates column: plasmids are whole contigs.
    if (nrow(genomad_plasmid) > 0) genomad_plasmid %>%
        mutate(origin = "Plasmid", coordinates = paste0("1-", length)) %>%
        select(seq_name, origin, coordinates, length, n_genes,
            any_of(c("plasmid_score", "conjugation_genes", "amr_genes"))) %>%
        rename(score = plasmid_score)
)

if (nrow(genomad_regions) > 0) {
    genomad_regions <- genomad_regions %>%
        separate(coordinates, into = c("genomad_start", "genomad_end"), 
            sep = "-", convert = TRUE, remove = FALSE)
} else {
    genomad_regions <- tibble(
        seq_name = character(), origin = character(),
        coordinates = character(), length = integer(),
        n_genes = integer(), score = numeric(),
        genomad_start = integer(), genomad_end = integer()
    )
}

#Metagraph
metagraph_raw <- fromJSON(snakemake@input[["metagraph"]], simplifyVector = FALSE)

metagraph_top <- map_dfr(metagraph_raw, function(entry) {
    querry <- entry$query_id
    results <- entry$raw_results$results

    if (length(results) == 0) {
        return(
            tibble(
                query = querry,
                sequence_id = NA_character_,
                organism = NA_character_,
                normalized_score = NA_real_,
                database = NA_character_,
                geo_loc_name = NA_character_,
                sequence_url = NA_character_,
                biosample = NA_character_
            )
        )
    }

    scores <- sapply(results, function(r) r$table_data$normalized_score)
    top <- results[[which.max(scores)]]

    tibble(
        query = querry,
        sequence_id = top$table_data$sequence_id,
        organism = top$table_data$organism,
        normalized_score = top$table_data$normalized_score,
        database = top$table_data$database,
        geo_loc_name = top$enrichment$geo_loc_name,
        sequence_url = top$table_data$sequence_url,
        biosample = top$table_data$biosample
    )
})

metagraph_all <- map_dfr(metagraph_raw, function(entry) {
    querry <- entry$query_id
    results <- entry$raw_results$results
    if (length(results) == 0) return(NULL)

    map_dfr(results, function(result) {
        tibble(
            query = querry,
            sequence_id = result$table_data$sequence_id,
            organism = result$table_data$organism,
            normalized_score = result$table_data$normalized_score,
            database = result$table_data$database,
            geo_loc_name = result$enrichment$geo_loc_name,
            sequence_url = result$table_data$sequence_url,
            biosample = result$table_data$biosample
        )
    })
})

# If MetaGraph returned nothing (no genes extracted, or every query failed), the tables above
# have no columns. Binding them to an empty template keeps the expected columns.
metagraph_template <- tibble(
    query = character(), sequence_id = character(), organism = character(),
    normalized_score = numeric(), database = character(), geo_loc_name = character(),
    sequence_url = character(), biosample = character()
)
metagraph_top <- bind_rows(metagraph_template, metagraph_top)
metagraph_all <- bind_rows(metagraph_template, metagraph_all)

n_metagraph_queried <- nrow(metagraph_top)
has_metagraph_hits  <- any(!is.na(metagraph_top$organism))
```

## Annotation results {.tabset .tabset-fade .tabset-pills}

Genome annotation combines two tools:

- **Bakta** (version `r bakta_version`, database `r db_version`) was used for bacterial genome annotation, identifying genomic features such as coding sequences (CDSs), tRNAs, rRNAs and other non-coding RNAs, and assigning gene names and product descriptions.
- **EggNOG-mapper** (version `r emapper_version`) was used for functional annotation of the protein sequences predicted by Bakta, assigning a seed ortholog with alignment metrics (percent identity, query and subject coverage), a COG functional category and a functional description.

### Overview

The following table summarizes the key features of the annotated genome, as reported by Bakta.

```{r bakta_overview}
# Create a summary table of genome features and display it.
tibble(
    Feature = c("Genome length", "GC content", "Coding density", "tRNAs",
        "tmRNAs", "rRNAs", "ncRNAs", "CDSs", "Pseudogenes",
        "Hypothetical proteins", "sORFs", "oriCs", "oriVs", "oriTs"),
    Value = c(genome_length, gc_content, coding_density, n_trna, n_tmrna,
        n_rrna, n_ncrna, n_cds, n_pseudogenes, n_hypothetical, n_sorf,
        n_orics, n_orivs, n_orits)
) %>%
    datatable(
        caption = "Genome annotation summary",
        filter   = "none",
        options  = list(pageLength = 20, dom = "t"),
        rownames = FALSE,
        class    = "cell-border stripe hover"
    )
```

### Gene annotation

The following table lists all annotated genes. Bakta results (sequence ID, locus tag, feature type, gene name and product) are joined with EggNOG-mapper results by locus tag, so both can be browsed and filtered together. Columns are prefixed with `Bakta:` or `EggNOG:` to show their source. Since EggNOG-mapper only annotates protein-coding genes, rows for other feature types (e.g. tRNAs, rRNAs) and proteins without an EggNOG hit have empty `EggNOG:` columns.

```{r annotation_table}
# Display the joined Bakta + EggNOG annotation table with interactive features for filtering and exporting.
bakta_eggnog_combined %>%
    datatable(
        caption = "Gene annotation (Bakta + EggNOG-mapper)",
        filter   = "top",
        extensions = "Buttons",
        options  = list(
            pageLength = 20,
            dom = "Blfrtip",
            buttons = c("copy", "csv","pdf"),
            scrollX = TRUE
        ),
        class    = "display"
    )
```

## ABRicate results {.tabset .tabset-fade .tabset-pills}

ABRicate was used to screen the assembled genome against multiple databases for antimicrobial resistance genes and plasmid replicons.
Genes were identified based on nucleotide sequence similarity with minimum coverage of `r abricate_mincov`% and minimum identity of `r abricate_minid`%.

### AMR genes

The summary table shows the presence of detected resistance genes across AMR databases (NCBI AMRFinderPlus, CARD, Resfinder).

```{r abricate_amr}
# Display the summary of AMR genes detected by ABRicate, excluding plasmid replicons, with interactive features for filtering and exporting.
abricate_amr_table <- abricate_summary %>%
    filter(Database != "PlasmidFinder") %>%
    select(-NUM_FOUND) %>%
    # Drop gene columns not found by any AMR database ("." = not found), e.g. plasmid replicons.
    select(where(~ !all(as.character(.x) %in% ".")))

# Only the Database column left means no AMR genes were found.
if (ncol(abricate_amr_table) > 1) {
    abricate_amr_table %>%
        kable(caption = "AMR genes detected by each database (% coverage)") %>%
        kableExtra::kable_styling(
            bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
            full_width = TRUE,
            font_size = 12
        ) %>%
        kableExtra::scroll_box(width = "100%")
} else {
    cat("No AMR genes detected by ABRicate.")
}
```

### Plasmid replicons

PlasmidFinder was used to identify plasmid replicon sequences, enabling classification of plasmid incompatibility types present in the genome.

```{r abricate_plasmid}
# Display the summary of plasmid replicons detected by ABRicate, with interactive features for filtering and exporting.
abricate_plasmid_table <- abricate_summary %>%
    filter(Database == "PlasmidFinder") %>%
    select(-NUM_FOUND) %>%
    # Drop gene columns not found by PlasmidFinder ("." = not found), e.g. AMR genes.
    select(where(~ !all(as.character(.x) %in% ".")))

# Only the Database column left means no plasmid replicons were found.
if (ncol(abricate_plasmid_table) > 1) {
    abricate_plasmid_table %>%
        kable(caption = "Plasmid replicons detected (% coverage)") %>%
        kableExtra::kable_styling(
            bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
            full_width = TRUE,
            font_size = 12
        ) %>%
        kableExtra::scroll_box(width = "100%")
} else {
    cat("No plasmid replicons detected by PlasmidFinder.")
}
```

## geNomad results

geNomad was used to identify sequences of viral and plasmid origin in the assembled genome.
The table below summarizes the detected mobile genetic element regions, including their predicted origin (virus or plasmid), genomic coordinates, length, number of genes, and confidence score.

```{r genomad_results}
# Display the geNomad detected regions with interactive features for filtering and exporting. If no regions were detected, display a message.
if (nrow(genomad_regions) > 0) {
    genomad_regions %>%
        select(seq_name, origin, coordinates, length, n_genes, score, 
            any_of(c("taxonomy", "conjugation_genes", "amr_genes"))) %>%
        datatable(
            caption = "geNomad detected regions",
            filter = "top",
            extensions = "Buttons",
            options = list(
                pageLength = 20,
                dom = "Blfrtip",
                buttons = c("copy", "csv", "pdf"),
                scrollX = TRUE
            ),
            class = "display"
        )
} else {
    cat("No viral or plasmid regions detected by geNomad.")
}
```

## Gene Map

Annotated genes from Bakta were visualised as gene arrow maps using the gggenes R package. 
The given sequence was divided into 30 kb windows to improve readability, with each window displayed as a separate panel. 
Arrow direction indicates the coding strand. Coloring highlights genes by their origin-related signal: AMR and resistance genes 
(based on ABRicate hits), defense mechanisms (COG category V), mobilome genes such as prophages and transposons (COG category X), 
plasmid regions (ABRicate replicons and geNomad), and prophage or viral regions (geNomad).

```{r gene_map_setup}
# Identify genes associated with COG category V (defense mechanisms) and COG category X (mobilome) from both Bakta annotations and EggNOG-mapper results.
cog_v_genes <- union(
    bakta_tsv %>% filter(str_detect(DbXrefs, "COG:V")) %>% pull(`Locus Tag`),
    eggnog_combined %>% filter(str_detect(COG_category, "V")) %>% pull(query)
)
cog_x_genes <- union(
    bakta_tsv %>% filter(str_detect(DbXrefs, "COG:X")) %>% pull(`Locus Tag`),
    eggnog_combined %>% filter(str_detect(COG_category, "X")) %>% pull(query)
)

# Extract AMR gene names from ABRicate summary for later use in gene classification
amr_gene_names <- abricate_summary %>%
    select(-Database, -NUM_FOUND) %>%
    names()

# Function to check if a gene is an AMR gene based on its name or product description matching known AMR gene names from ABRicate summary.
is_amr_gene <- function(gene, product, amr_names) {
    gene_l <- tolower(gene)
    product_l <- tolower(product)
    any(sapply(tolower(amr_names), function(a) {
        grepl(a, gene_l, fixed = TRUE) | grepl(a, product_l, fixed = TRUE)
    }))
}

window_size <- 30000
windows_per_plot <- 40

# Prepare gene data for plotting, including classification based on COG categories, ABRicate hits, and geNomad regions.
gene_data <- bakta_tsv %>%
    left_join(
        eggnog_combined %>% select(query, COG_category, Description),
        by = c("Locus Tag" = "query")
    ) %>%
    mutate(
        forward = Strand == "+",
        is_cog_v = `Locus Tag` %in% cog_v_genes,
        is_cog_x = `Locus Tag` %in% cog_x_genes,
        is_amr = map2_lgl(Start, Stop, function(s, e) {
            any(abricate_hits_amr$START < e & abricate_hits_amr$END > s)
        }),
        is_plasmid_rep = map2_lgl(Start, Stop, function(s, e) {
            any(abricate_hits_plasmid$START < e & abricate_hits_plasmid$END > s)
        }),
        is_viral = map2_lgl(Start, Stop, function(s, e) {
            any(genomad_regions$origin == "Virus" & 
                genomad_regions$genomad_start < e & 
                genomad_regions$genomad_end > s)
        }),
        is_plasmid = map2_lgl(Start, Stop, function(s, e) {
            any(genomad_regions$origin == "Plasmid" & 
                genomad_regions$genomad_start < e & 
                genomad_regions$genomad_end > s)
        }),
        highlight = case_when(
            is_amr            ~ "AMR / resistance",
            is_cog_v          ~ "Defense (COG V)",
            is_cog_x          ~ "Mobilome (COG X)",
            is_plasmid_rep | is_plasmid ~ "Plasmid",
            is_viral          ~ "Prophage / viral",
            TRUE              ~ "Other"
        ),
        highlight = factor(highlight, 
            levels = c("AMR / resistance", "Defense (COG V)", "Mobilome (COG X)", "Plasmid", "Prophage / viral", "Other")),
        tooltip = paste0(
            "<b>", coalesce(Gene, "-"), "</b> (", `Locus Tag`, ")",
            "<br>Type: ", Type,
            "<br>Product: ", Product,
            "<br>COG category: ", coalesce(COG_category, "-"),
            "<br>EggNOG description: ", coalesce(Description, "-")
        ),
        midpoint = (Start + Stop) / 2,
        window_num = floor(midpoint / window_size),
        plot_batch = floor(window_num / windows_per_plot) + 1,
        molecule = paste0(
            format(window_num * window_size / 1e6, nsmall = 1), " – ",
            format((window_num + 1) * window_size / 1e6, nsmall = 1), " Mb"
        ),
        molecule = reorder(molecule, window_num)
    )

batches <- sort(unique(gene_data$plot_batch))

highlight_colors <- c(
    "AMR / resistance"     = "#FB8500",
    "Defense (COG V)"      = "#1c7f97",
    "Mobilome (COG X)"     = "#588157",
    "Plasmid"              = "#A855F7",
    "Prophage / viral"     = "#E63946",
    "Other"                = "#cccccc"
)
```
```{r gene_map, results='asis', fig.height=32, fig.width=12}
# Generate gene maps for each batch of windows, creating interactive plots with ggiraph. Each plot is displayed as a separate panel in the report.
for (b in batches) {
  batch_data <- gene_data %>% filter(plot_batch == b)
  n_win <- length(unique(batch_data$molecule))
  h <- max(n_win * 1.5, 4)

  p <- ggplot(batch_data, aes(xmin = Start, xmax = Stop, y = molecule,
    fill = highlight, forward = forward)) +
    geom_gene_arrow(arrowhead_height = unit(4, "mm"), arrow_body_height = unit(3, "mm")) +
    geom_rect_interactive(
      aes(xmin = Start, xmax = Stop,
          ymin = 0.6, ymax = 1.4,
          tooltip = tooltip,
          data_id = `Locus Tag`),
      fill = "transparent", colour = "transparent"
    ) +
    facet_wrap(~ molecule, scales = "free", ncol = 1) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = highlight_colors, name = NULL, drop = FALSE) +
    theme_genes() +
    theme(
        strip.text = element_text(size = 12, margin = margin(1, 0, 1, 0)),
        plot.text = element_text(size = 12),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 12),
        panel.spacing = unit(0.1, "lines")
    ) +
    labs(x = "Position (bp)", y = NULL)

  widget <- girafe(
    ggobj = p,
    width_svg = 12, height_svg = h,
    options = list(
      opts_tooltip(css = "background:white;padding:8px;border-radius:4px;border:1px solid #ccc;font-size:12px;"),
      opts_hover(css = "fill:orange;stroke:orange;opacity:0.5;"),
      opts_sizing(rescale = TRUE, width = 1)
    )
  )

  cat(knitr::knit_child(text = c(
    sprintf("```{r gene-map-%d, echo=FALSE, fig.height=%g, fig.width=12}", b, h),
    "widget",
    "```"
  ), envir = environment(), quiet = TRUE))
  cat("\n\n")
}
```

## Metagraph results

MetaGraph was used to query the selected origin-related gene set — comprising COG category V (defense mechanism) 
and COG category X (mobilome) genes, together with AMR and plasmid genes identified by ABRicate and viral and plasmid genes 
identified by geNomad — against a large-scale sequence search index to identify the closest matching organisms. 
For each gene, the top hit was selected based on the highest normalized alignment score. 
Results include the matched organism, database source, geographic location of the sample, and sequence accession.

```{r metagraph_status, results='asis'}
# Explain why the MetaGraph tables below are empty, if they are.
if (n_metagraph_queried == 0) {
    cat("**No genes were queried in MetaGraph**: no COG V/X, AMR, plasmid or viral genes were found in this sample, or all MetaGraph queries failed.\n")
} else if (!has_metagraph_hits) {
    cat(sprintf("**None of the %d queried genes had MetaGraph hits.**\n", n_metagraph_queried))
}
```

### Overview {.tabset .tabset-fade .tabset-pills}

#### Hits quality

`r if (!has_metagraph_hits) "No MetaGraph hits to show."`

```{r metagraph_quality, eval = has_metagraph_hits}
# Plot the distribution of normalized scores for the top hits, excluding genes with no hits (NA scores). This provides an overview of the quality of matches found by MetaGraph.
metagraph_top %>%
    filter(!is.na(normalized_score)) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = normalized_score)) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "#219EBC", colour = "white", alpha = 0.8) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = 5), 
        labels = function(x) format(x, big.mark = "", decimal.mark = "")) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
    ) +
    labs(x = "Normalized score", y = "Number of genes",
         title = "Distribution of top hit scores")
```

#### Top organisms

`r if (!has_metagraph_hits) "No MetaGraph hits to show."`

```{r metagraph_organisms, eval = has_metagraph_hits}
# Summarize the top matched organisms based on MetaGraph results, filtering out non-specific matches (e.g., metagenomes, generic "bacterium" entries)
# The summary includes the number of distinct genes matched, total hits, and mean score for each organism.
top_n_organism <- 20

organism_stats <- metagraph_all %>%
    filter(!is.na(organism)) %>%
    filter(!str_detect(organism, regex("metagenome", ignore_case = TRUE))) %>%
    filter(!str_detect(organism, "bacterium")) %>%
    group_by(organism) %>%
    summarise(
        n_genes = n_distinct(query),
        n_hits = n(),
        mean_score = mean(normalized_score),
        .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    arrange(desc(n_genes)) %>%
    mutate(organism = if_else(row_number() > top_n_organism, "Other", organism)) %>%
    group_by(organism) %>%
    summarise(
        n_genes = sum(n_genes),
        n_hits = sum(n_hits),
        mean_score = mean(mean_score),
        .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    filter(organism != "Other") %>%
    arrange(n_genes) %>%
    mutate(organism = factor(organism, levels = organism))

top_organisms <- organism_stats %>% pull(organism)

gene_details <- metagraph_all %>%
    filter(!is.na(organism), organism %in% top_organisms) %>%
    filter(!str_detect(organism, regex("metagenome", ignore_case = TRUE))) %>%
    filter(!str_detect(organism, "bacterium")) %>%
    group_by(organism, query) %>%
    slice_max(order_by = normalized_score, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    select(organism, query, normalized_score)

shared_genes <- SharedData$new(gene_details, key = ~organism, group = "organism_link")
shared_data <- SharedData$new(organism_stats, key = ~organism, group = "organism_link")
```

```{r metagraph_organisms_plot, eval = has_metagraph_hits}
# Create an interactive bar plot of the top matched organisms, showing the number of distinct genes matched and coloring by mean score.
# The plot allows users to select organisms and see the corresponding genes in the linked data table below.
plot_ly(shared_data, x = ~n_genes, y = ~organism, type = "bar", orientation = "h",
    marker = list(
        color = ~mean_score, 
        colorscale = "Plasma",
        colorbar = list(title = "Mean Score")
    ),
    text = ~paste0(n_genes, " genes (", n_hits, " hits)")) %>%
    layout(
        title = "Top matched organisms",
        xaxis = list(title = "Number of distinct genes matched"),
        yaxis = list(title = "", categoryorder = "trace"),
        dragmode = "select",
        height = 500
    )
```

```{r metagraph_organisms_table, eval = has_metagraph_hits}
# Display a data table of the genes matched to the top organisms, showing the organism name, gene query, and normalized score.
# The table is linked to the bar plot above, allowing users to see which genes are associated with each organism when selected.
datatable(shared_genes,
    colnames = c("Organism", "Gene", "Score"),
    options = list(pageLength = 15, scrollY = "400px"),
    rownames = FALSE
)
```

### Hits {.tabset .tabset-fade .tabset-pills}

#### Top hits per gene

`r if (!has_metagraph_hits) "No MetaGraph hits to show."`

```{r metagraph_top_hits, eval = has_metagraph_hits}
# Display the top MetaGraph hits for each gene, filtering out genes with no hits (NA organisms). 
metagraph_top %>%
    filter(!is.na(organism)) %>%
    datatable(
        caption = "Top Metagraph hits for each gene",
        filter   = "top",
        extensions = "Buttons",
        options  = list(
            pageLength = 20,
            dom = "Blfrtip",
            buttons = c("copy", "csv","pdf"),
            scrollX = TRUE
        ),
        class    = "display"
    )
```

#### All hits

`r if (!has_metagraph_hits) "No MetaGraph hits to show."`

```{r metagraph_all_hits, eval = has_metagraph_hits}
# Display all MetaGraph hits for each gene, filtering out genes with no hits (NA organisms) and sorting by query and normalized score.
metagraph_all %>%
    filter(!is.na(organism)) %>%
    arrange(query, desc(normalized_score)) %>%
    datatable(
        caption = "All Metagraph hits for each gene",
        filter   = "top",
        extensions = "Buttons",
        options  = list(
            pageLength = 20,
            dom = "Blfrtip",
            buttons = c("copy", "csv","pdf"),
            scrollX = TRUE
        ),
        class    = "display"
    )
```

#### No-hit genes

`r if (n_metagraph_queried == 0) "No genes were queried in MetaGraph."`

```{r metagraph_no_hits, eval = n_metagraph_queried > 0}
# Display genes that had no hits in MetaGraph (NA organisms), indicating they may be novel or highly divergent.
metagraph_top %>%
    filter(is.na(organism)) %>%
    datatable(
        caption = "Genes with no Metagraph hits",
        filter   = "top",
        extensions = "Buttons",
        options  = list(
            pageLength = 20,
            dom = "Blfrtip",
            buttons = c("copy", "csv","pdf"),
            scrollX = TRUE
        ),
        class    = "display"
    )
```
